title: signin.v1
description: Who may sign in, and who may become the administrator: the internal wire between the terminal's server (the sign-in doors) and admin-api (which holds every input and decides). The terminal asks and obeys; it holds no list of its own. Internal tier only (X-Internal-Secret). The reason vocabularies are the contract: the terminal's TypeScript and admin-api's Python both read them from code generated from this file (gen.mjs), so a reason one side adds is a reason the other side knows.

AdmittedReason.description: Why a sign-in was admitted. admin: the claimed role is on this user. admin-email: VEXA_ADMIN_EMAILS names this address. existing-user: an account exists. allow-list: VEXA_SIGNIN_ALLOW or the admin-edited signin.allow setting matches. claim-code: the instance is unclaimed, nothing is configured, and this sign-in carries the live admin claim code.

RefusedReason.description: Why a sign-in was refused. not-allowed covers every refusal on purpose: the answer must not tell a caller which list an address is missing from.

ClaimReason.description: Why the admin role was or was not handed over. claimed: this user is now the administrator. admin-exists: a user holds the role, or VEXA_ADMIN_EMAILS names the admins. bad-code: no admin claim code, a wrong one, or a spent one. not-allowed: an allow-list is configured and this address is not on it.

ClaimCode.description: The one-time admin claim code as a person typed it. admin-api folds case, separators and O/I/L before comparing; the canonical form is XXXX-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX in Crockford base32.

SigninAdmissionRequest.description: POST /internal/signin-admission — may this address sign in? Asked by every terminal door before anything is created or mailed.

email.description: The address, as the door received it. admin-api lower-cases and trims it.

SigninAdmissionResponse.description: The verdict. A caller admits only on a literal admitted:true with an AdmittedReason; anything else, including a body that does not conform, refuses.

AdminClaimRequest.description: POST /internal/bootstrap-admin — make this user the administrator, if admin-api's claim rule allows it.

user_id.description: The admin-api user id, as the validate oracle returned it.

admin_exists.description: Whether the instance has an administrator after this call.

ClaimCodeCheckRequest.description: POST /internal/admin-claim/check — is this the live admin claim code? The claim screen asks before a sign-in carries it.

valid.description: True only while the claim is open and the code is the live one.

InstanceState.description: GET /internal/instance — does this instance have an administrator (a claimed one, or addresses VEXA_ADMIN_EMAILS names)?

SigninLinkRedeemRequest.description: POST /internal/signin-links/redeem — the terminal redeems an emailed sign-in link it has verified (signature and expiry are the terminal's own check). admin-api records the link's jti in the service Redis until it expires, so a link signs in once across every terminal replica and restart. 200 with SigninLinkRedeemResponse the first time; 409 when the jti was already redeemed (or has expired); 503 when the record cannot be written, which the terminal answers by refusing the sign-in.

jti.description: The link's random id (a UUID as the terminal mints it).

expires_at.description: The link's own expiry, epoch seconds; the record is kept until then.

first.description: This redemption is the link's first.

ProviderSubjectBindRequest.description: PUT /internal/users/{id}/provider-subject — the terminal binds the account a Google or Microsoft sign-in reached to that identity's stable subject, before it mints a token. The first sign-in through a provider records the subject; a later one must carry the same (200 ProviderSubjectBindResponse), and one with another subject is refused with 409, changing nothing. 404 for an unknown account.

bound.description: first: this sign-in bound the provider; same: it was already bound to this subject.
